title: Guwahati
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
info: Kamakhya Temple, gateway to North-East India
body:
Guwahati is the largest city in Assam and the main gateway to North-East India. It stands on the south bank of the Brahmaputra river, in the Kamrup Metropolitan district.

Landmarks

The Kamakhya Temple, on Nilachal Hill, is one of the most important Shakti temples in India and draws pilgrims especially during the Ambubachi Mela. Other well-known places include Umananda Island — the smallest inhabited river island in the world — the Assam State Museum, and the Brahmaputra riverfront.

Today

Guwahati is Assam's main commercial, educational and transport hub, with the Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, railway links across India, and universities including Gauhati University and IIT Guwahati nearby.
extra:
History

Known in ancient times as Pragjyotishpura, Guwahati was the capital of the Kamarupa kingdom. Its name is said to come from guva (areca nut) and hati (market rows).

Transport

Guwahati is connected by air (Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport), by rail (Guwahati and Kamakhya stations) and by road, and the Saraighat Bridge was the first rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra in the region.

Education

The city hosts Gauhati University, Cotton University, IIT Guwahati (at Amingaon, across the river), and many colleges, making it the educational hub of the North-East.
